FOREWORD

This Indian Standard (Part 2) which is identical with IS0 6987-2 :1990 `Indexable inserts for cutting tools - Hardmetal (carbide) inserts with rounded corners, with partly cylindrical fixing hole - Part 2 : Dimensions of inserts with 1 lo normal clearance' issued by the International. Organization for Standardization (ISO) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on the recommendations of the Single Point Cutting Tools, Carbide Tips and Indexable Inserts Sectional Committee and approval of the Production Engineering Division Council. The text of the IS0 standard has been approved as suitable for publication as Indian Standard without deviations. Certain conventions are, however, not identical to those used in Indian Standards. Indian Standard
INDEXABLE INSERTS FOR CUTTING TOOLS HARDMETAL (CARBIDE) INSERTS WITH ROUNDED CORNERS, WITH PARTLY CYLINDRICAL FIXING HOLE
PART 2 DIMENSIONS OF INSERTS WITH 11' NORMAL CLEARANCE

1

Scope

- CP: rhombic inserts, with 11CJ normal clearance and 60' included angle; RP: round inserts, with ll" normal clearance.

This part of IS0 6967 specifies the dimensions of indexable hardmetal (carbide) inserts with rounded corners, with a partly cylindrical fixing hole and with 11" normal clearance. These inserts are primarily intended to be mounted on tools by a countersunk head screw or any other fixing element, such as a pin lock.

Inserts dealt with in this part of IS0 6967 are standardized without chip breakers (designated by the letter WI and with chip breakers on the face (designated by the letter T). At present, neither the shape nor the dimensions of chip breakers are standardized. Thus, if necessary, special features have to be explained with a diagram or additional specifications. Table C.l gives the range of sizes for these inserts.

2

Normative

references

The following standards contain provisions which, through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this part of IS0 6967. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision, and parties to agreements based on this part of IS0 6967 are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of the standards indicated below. Members of IEC and IS0 maintain registers of currently valid International Standards. 4 4.1

Interchangeability Tolerances

The indexable hardmetal (carbide) inserts which are the subject of this part of IS0 6%' are provided in tolerance class M, in accordance with IS0 1632. The values of the tolerances in accordance with IS0 1632 are given in annex A. Other tolerances are included in table 1 for hole dimensions, and in tables 3 to 5 for the corner radii rE.

3

Types

of inserts

The types of indexable hardmetal (carbide) inserts specified in this part of IS0 6967 are the following : TP : triangular inserts, with 1lo normal clearance; SP : square inserts, with 1lo normal clearance;

Thickness

s of inserts with chip breaker

The thickness s of inserts with chip breaks% is defined as the distance between the cutting edge at the corner and the opposing supporting surface of the insert; see figures 1 a) and 1 b).

Measurement

Recommended

dimensions

- the symbol of the group of application, in accordance with IS0 513;
the commercial designation of the hardmetal (carbide) grade. -

The choice of the more common dimensions is restricted to the values given in tables 3 to 6. It is strongly recommended that these standard inserts be used wherever possible (first preference). When other inserts are required, their dimensions shall be selected from the non-shaded areas of table C.l (second preference). Inserts having dimensions given in the
shaded areas of this table are ndt recommended. NOTE - The m-dimensions are calculated using the exact values of the corner radius rs given in table 2, rounded to the third decimal place.

Annex

B

(normative)
Methods of measurement of dimension

m

B.l

Triangular

inserts

8.3

Rhombic

inserts

Dimension 112 is related to the side opposite the corner that is to be measured. The insert is placed on a surface plate as shown in figure B. 1 and checked by means of a dial gauge zeroed with the aid of a gauge block corresponding to dimension m. The dial gauge then gives a direct reading of the error when applied to the inserts to be measured.

Dimension m is checked by reference to the diameter d of a precision roller, where d corresponds to the nominal diameter of the inscribed circle of the insert. The insert is mounted on an W or 1CW vee-block as shown in figure 8.3 and checked by means of a dial gauge which has been zeroed to dimension m by means of a roller with the aid of a gauge block. The dial gauge then gives a direct reading of the error when applied to the inserts to be measured.

Figure B.l

Figure 8.3

B.2

Square inserts

B.4

Round inserts

Dimension m is checked by reference to the diameter d of a precision roller, where d corresponds to the nominal diameter of the inscribed circle of the insert. The insert is mounted on a !W vee-block as shown in figure 8.2 and checked by means of a dial gauge which has been zeroed to dimension m by means of a roller with the aid of a gauge block. The dial gauge then gives a direct reading of the error when applied to the inserts to be measured.

The diameter d is measured with a micrometer or a similar device.

Figure 8.2
